title: Every word card the same shape
statement: Give every word card the same shape: when pictures fit only a few taught words, use none, since uneven cards signal that some words are harder or different.
example: Pictures could cover only 3 of a course's 70 taught words, most of them abstract, so every card went text-only.
detail: A review of a Grade 3 reading course asked that pictures be removed from all word cards if they could not cover every word. At that point illustrations could cover only 3 of the course's 70 taught words, dominated by abstract words that resist illustration, so the ruling made every card text-only everywhere. The stated reason is that inconsistent cards signal to the child that some words are harder or different in kind.
against: The rule gives up pictures even where they seem helpful, and nothing measured whether text-only cards teach words better.

evidence.quote: every card must be the same shape; images are not added to any card even when they seem helpful.

illustrations can cover only a small minority of them (only 3 of 70 at the point the rule was triggered), dominated by abstract words that resist illustration; inconsistent cards signal to the child that some words are harder or different in kind.
Text-only is adopted everywhere for consistency.
if images can't cover all words, remove them from all pages for consistency
